evals.prompt: The voice in this talking-head video goes up and down in volume — some lines are loud, some are really quiet. Can you even that out?
evals.expected_output: Should identify this as an internal-loudness-range problem, not an overall-level problem. Should measure LRA with ebur128 first, apply speechnorm to compress loud parts and lift quiet parts, verify the resulting LRA dropped into roughly the 3-5 LU range, then apply a final linear loudnorm gain (using measured values, not another dynamic pass) to land at a safe target level and peak. Should copy the video stream rather than re-encoding it.
assertions: Distinguishes this from a simple overall-loudness normalization
Measures loudness range (LRA) before and after
Uses speechnorm (or equivalent dynamics processing) rather than only loudnorm linear mode
Applies the final gain as a linear/measured pass rather than stacking a second dynamic normalizer
Uses -c:v copy so the video isn't needlessly re-encoded

evals.prompt: This whole video's audio is just too quiet compared to my other videos, can you fix the level?
evals.expected_output: Should recognize this as an overall-level problem rather than an internal-consistency problem, and reach for a two-pass loudnorm (measure then linear apply) to hit a target integrated loudness, without necessarily needing speechnorm if the loudness range is already reasonable. Should still check LRA to confirm there isn't also an internal-consistency issue worth mentioning.
assertions: Recognizes this as primarily an overall-level issue, not necessarily requiring speechnorm
Uses a measured/linear loudnorm pass to hit a specific target loudness
Checks LRA rather than assuming no internal inconsistency exists
